_comment: SETUP-ONLY permissions to finish SES/SNS bounce monitoring. Attach to IAM user
mcaffeine-erp-prefg-tool in account 157320387454 as its own policy, alongside
iam-policy-erp-app-runtime-ses.json and iam-policy-erp-app-deploy.json.
The running app needs NONE of this. It only sends mail (runtime-ses) and
receives events on POST /api/v1/webhooks/ses, which is unauthenticated to AWS
and gated by the SNS signature check instead. This policy exists so the
monitoring can be CONFIGURED, and can be detached again afterwards.
ALREADY DONE, needs nothing further:
- SES configuration set 'erp-app' publishes BOUNCE, COMPLAINT, DELIVERY,
DELIVERY_DELAY, REJECT, RENDERING_FAILURE to topic erp-app-ses-events.
- That topic has a CONFIRMED https subscription to
https://erp.mcaffeine.com/api/v1/webhooks/ses, verified end to end via the
SES bounce simulator on 2026-08-31.
- The subscription's retry policy is 18 attempts, 20s -> 300s exponential.
Note SNS caps TOTAL retry time at 3600s, so this is close to the maximum;
a longer outage than an hour still loses events, which is what the DLQ
below is for.
STILL OUTSTANDING, and what each statement here unblocks:
1. Queue erp-app-ses-events-dlq EXISTS but has no access policy, so SNS
cannot write to it. sqs:SetQueueAttributes is the missing piece; until it
lands, attaching a redrive policy would look configured while still
dropping messages, so the redrive has deliberately been left off.
2. No CloudWatch alarms on SES at all. The account has only a disk-usage and
an EC2 status-check alarm.
The three alarms to create, all actioned to the existing Email_ALert topic:
erp-ses-bounce-rate         AWS/SES Reputation.BounceRate    > 0.05
erp-ses-complaint-rate      AWS/SES Reputation.ComplaintRate > 0.001
erp-ses-events-undelivered  AWS/SNS NumberOfNotificationsFailed > 0
The last read-only statement is not incidental: the alarms point at
Email_ALert and nobody has confirmed it has a subscriber. An alarm topic with
no subscriber is the exact failure this whole exercise uncovered on
erp-app-ses-events - bounces published for months to a topic nobody read.
Remove this _comment key before attaching; IAM rejects unknown top-level keys.
